questions.stem: Ravi ran 9 km 857 m on Saturday and Siti ran 3 km 371 m. What is the total distance of the two, in km and m?

explain.why: Did not change 1000 m to 1 km.
Made a slip adding the m.
Left 1228 m without changing to km.

questions.stem: Shu Fen's bag of rice has a mass of 7 kg 68 g and Ravi's bag has a mass of 1 kg 168 g. Find the difference between the two amounts. Give your answer in kg and g.

explain.why: Made a slip in the g.
Took 68 g from 168 g the wrong way round.
Did not take 1 kg away after regrouping.

questions.stem: Shu Fen has 18 packets of flour of mass 135 g each. What is the total in kg and g?

explain.why: Used 1 kg = 100 g.
Left the answer as 2430 g.
Lost a digit in the small part.

questions.stem: A total of 24 m 30 cm is divided equally into 6 parts. How many cm are in each part?

explain.why: Divided by 7.
Divided only the 24 m and added the 30 cm.
Divided by 5.

questions.stem: Daniel's full tin of biscuits has a total mass of 2.2 kg. After 1/4 of the contents are used, the total mass is 1.7 kg. What is the mass of the empty container, in grams?

explain.why: Used the number of parts left instead of the whole.
Used the mass after using some contents as the empty mass.
Multiplied the used mass by 1/4 instead of dividing.

solution: 1/4 of contents = 500 g, so contents = 2000 g

questions.stem: A jug contains 4 l 950 ml of water. Shu Fen fills as many glasses of 200 ml as possible. How many glasses are filled completely?

explain.why: Used 1 l = 100 ml.
Made a slip in the division.
Counted the glass that is only partly filled.

questions.stem: The lengths of four things in Shu Fen's pencil case are: ribbon 37 cm, eraser 25 cm, crayon 58 cm and pencil 14 cm. Which is the second shortest?

explain.why: Counted from the wrong end of the ordered list.
Gave the shortest instead of the second.
Gave the item at the other end of the list.

solution: Order from shortest to longest: 14 cm, 25 cm, 37 cm, 58 cm.
The second shortest is the eraser, 25 cm.

questions.stem: Shu Fen has a leaf that is 50 cm long, a spring that is 42 cm long and a ribbon that is 24 cm long. How much longer is the leaf than the ribbon, in cm?

explain.why: Added the two lengths.
Compared the shortest with the middle one.
Compared the longest with the middle one.

questions.stem: Wei Jie measures a strip of paper with a ruler but starts from a mark that is not 0, as shown. What is the length of the strip of paper to the nearest cm?

explain.why: Read the right end of the line without subtracting the start mark.
Counted one gap too few or too many.
Rounded to the wrong whole number of centimetres.

solution: The line starts at 2 cm. Its right end is at about 9.9 cm.
Length = 9.9 - 2 = 7.9 cm, which is 8 cm to the nearest cm.

questions.stem: Shu Fen measures four lines, A to D, with a ruler. Which line is exactly 5 cm long?

explain.why: Read the end mark (it is 5) without subtracting where the line starts.
Picked the line that is 6 cm long.
Picked the line that is 4 cm long.

solution: Length = right end - left end for each line.
Only line A has right end - left end = 5 cm.

questions.stem: Hui Min's bag of rice has a mass of 2 kg 981 g and Daniel's bag has a mass of 6 kg 36 g. What is the total mass of the two, in kg and g?

explain.why: Left 1017 g without changing to kg.
Did not change 1000 g to 1 kg.
Made a slip adding the g.

questions.stem: Hui Min's bag of rice has a mass of 9 kg 170 g and Ravi's bag has a mass of 6 kg 313 g. Find the difference between the two amounts. Give your answer in kg and g.

explain.why: Took 170 g from 313 g the wrong way round.
Made a slip in the g.
Did not take 1 kg away after regrouping.

questions.stem: Wei Jie has 6 packets of flour of mass 305 g each. What is the total in kg and g?

explain.why: Lost a digit in the small part.
Used 1 kg = 100 g.
Left the answer as 1830 g.

questions.stem: A total of 1 kg 740 g is divided equally into 3 parts. How many g are in each part?

explain.why: Put a zero in the wrong place.
Divided by 2.
Divided by 4.

questions.stem: Arjun's full tin of biscuits has a total mass of 1.1 kg. After 3/4 of the contents are used, the total mass is 0.5 kg. What is the mass of the empty container, in grams?

explain.why: Used the number of parts left instead of the whole.
Multiplied the used mass by 3/4 instead of dividing.
Used the mass after using some contents as the empty mass.

solution: 3/4 of contents = 600 g, so contents = 800 g

questions.stem: A jug contains 3 l 650 ml of water. Ravi fills as many glasses of 120 ml as possible. How many glasses are filled completely?

explain.why: Counted the glass that is only partly filled.
Made a slip in the division.
Used 1 l = 100 ml.

questions.stem: The lengths of four things in Hui Min's pencil case are: eraser 42 cm, strip of paper 48 cm, leaf 30 cm and crayon 22 cm. Which is the second shortest?

explain.why: Counted from the wrong end of the ordered list.
Gave the shortest instead of the second.
Gave the item at the other end of the list.

solution: Order from shortest to longest: 22 cm, 30 cm, 42 cm, 48 cm.
The second shortest is the leaf, 30 cm.

questions.stem: Siti has a wire that is 36 cm long, a string that is 17 cm long and a stick that is 12 cm long. How much longer is the wire than the stick, in cm?

explain.why: Added the two lengths.
Compared the longest with the middle one.
Compared the shortest with the middle one.

questions.stem: Shu Fen measures a strip of paper with a ruler but starts from a mark that is not 0, as shown. What is the length of the strip of paper to the nearest cm?

explain.why: Rounded to the wrong whole number of centimetres.
Counted one gap too few or too many.
Read the right end of the line without subtracting the start mark.

solution: The line starts at 2 cm. Its right end is at about 6.8 cm.
Length = 6.8 - 2 = 4.8 cm, which is 5 cm to the nearest cm.

explain.why: Read the end mark (it is 9) without subtracting where the line starts.
Picked the line that is 10 cm long.
Picked the line that is 8 cm long.

solution: Length = right end - left end for each line.
Only line D has right end - left end = 9 cm.

explain.why: Made a slip adding the cm.
Did not change 100 cm to 1 m.
Made a slip adding the cm.

questions.stem: Kumar ran 8 km 338 m on Saturday and Jun Wei ran 3 km 361 m. Find the difference between the two amounts. Give your answer in km and m.

explain.why: Did not take 1 km away after regrouping.
Made a slip in the m.
Took 338 m from 361 m the wrong way round.

questions.stem: Siti has 14 bottles of drink holding 355 ml each. What is the total in l and ml?

explain.why: Lost a digit in the small part.
Left the answer as 4970 ml.
Used 1 l = 100 ml.

questions.stem: A total of 3 l 430 ml is divided equally into 7 parts. How many ml are in each part?

explain.why: Divided by 8.
Divided by 6.
Put a zero in the wrong place.

questions.stem: Nurul's full jar of honey has a total mass of 3 kg. After 3/4 of the contents are used, the total mass is 0.9 kg. What is the mass of the empty container, in grams?

explain.why: Multiplied the used mass by 3/4 instead of dividing.
Used the number of parts left instead of the whole.
Used the mass after using some contents as the empty mass.

solution: 3/4 of contents = 2100 g, so contents = 2800 g

questions.stem: A jug contains 2 l 500 ml of water. Ravi fills as many glasses of 350 ml as possible. How many glasses are filled completely?

explain.why: Counted the glass that is only partly filled.
Made a slip in the division.
Used 1 l = 100 ml.

questions.stem: The lengths of four things in Kumar's pencil case are: scarf 41 cm, bookmark 39 cm, stick 51 cm and pencil 14 cm. Which is the second shortest?

explain.why: Gave the item at the other end of the list.
Gave the shortest instead of the second.
Counted from the wrong end of the ordered list.

solution: Order from shortest to longest: 14 cm, 39 cm, 41 cm, 51 cm.
The second shortest is the bookmark, 39 cm.

questions.stem: Kumar has a string that is 56 cm long, a ruler that is 42 cm long and a leaf that is 41 cm long. How much longer is the string than the leaf, in cm?

explain.why: Compared the longest with the middle one.
Compared the shortest with the middle one.
Added the two lengths.

questions.stem: Wei Jie measures a twig with a ruler but starts from a mark that is not 0, as shown. What is the length of the twig to the nearest cm?

explain.why: Counted one gap too few or too many.
Misread the end mark.
Rounded to the wrong whole number of centimetres.

solution: The line starts at 1 cm. Its right end is at about 9.3 cm.
Length = 9.3 - 1 = 8.3 cm, which is 8 cm to the nearest cm.

explain.why: Read the end mark (it is 5) without subtracting where the line starts.
Picked the line that is 6 cm long.
Picked the line that is 4 cm long.

solution: Length = right end - left end for each line.
Only line D has right end - left end = 5 cm.

questions.stem: Hui Min's ribbon is 1 m 22 cm long and Siti's ribbon is 2 m 88 cm long. What is the total length of the two, in m and cm?

explain.why: Made a slip adding the cm.
Left 110 cm without changing to m.
Did not change 100 cm to 1 m.

questions.stem: Wei Jie's ribbon is 9 m 10 cm long and Aisha's ribbon is 5 m 42 cm long. Find the difference between the two amounts. Give your answer in m and cm.

explain.why: Made a slip in the cm.
Took 10 cm from 42 cm the wrong way round.
Did not take 1 m away after regrouping.

questions.stem: Siti has 14 packets of flour of mass 115 g each. What is the total in kg and g?

explain.why: Lost a digit in the small part.
Left the answer as 1610 g.
Used 1 kg = 100 g.

questions.stem: A total of 6 m 40 cm is divided equally into 4 parts. How many cm are in each part?

explain.why: Divided only the 6 m and added the 40 cm.
Divided by 3.
Divided by 5.

questions.stem: Hui Min's full pot of soup has a total mass of 0.65 kg. After 1/2 of the contents are used, the total mass is 0.45 kg. What is the mass of the empty container, in grams?

explain.why: Used the mass after using some contents as the empty mass.
Multiplied the used mass by 1/2 instead of dividing.
Made a slip in the subtraction.

solution: 1/2 of contents = 200 g, so contents = 400 g

questions.stem: A jug contains 5 l 450 ml of water. Ali fills as many glasses of 250 ml as possible. How many glasses are filled completely?

explain.why: Made a slip in the division.
Counted the glass that is only partly filled.
Used 1 l = 100 ml.

questions.stem: The lengths of four things in Arjun's pencil case are: scarf 14 cm, strip of paper 30 cm, ruler 19 cm and spring 46 cm. Which is the second shortest?

explain.why: Gave the shortest instead of the second.
Counted from the wrong end of the ordered list.
Gave the item at the other end of the list.

solution: Order from shortest to longest: 14 cm, 19 cm, 30 cm, 46 cm.
The second shortest is the ruler, 19 cm.

questions.stem: Wei Jie has a straw that is 52 cm long, a string that is 28 cm long and a spring that is 30 cm long. How much longer is the straw than the string, in cm?

explain.why: Added the two lengths.
Compared the shortest with the middle one.
Compared the longest with the middle one.

questions.stem: Nurul measures a twig with a ruler but starts from a mark that is not 0, as shown. What is the length of the twig to the nearest cm?

explain.why: Counted one gap too few or too many.
Read the right end of the line without subtracting the start mark.
Rounded to the wrong whole number of centimetres.

solution: The line starts at 4 cm. Its right end is at about 8.9 cm.
Length = 8.9 - 4 = 4.9 cm, which is 5 cm to the nearest cm.

explain.why: Read the end mark (it is 4) without subtracting where the line starts.
Picked the line that is 5 cm long.
Picked the line that is 3 cm long.

solution: Length = right end - left end for each line.
Only line B has right end - left end = 4 cm.

explain.why: Did not change 1000 m to 1 km.
Made a slip adding the m.
Left 1611 m without changing to km.

questions.stem: Kumar ran 7 km 413 m on Saturday and Jun Wei ran 4 km 605 m. Find the difference between the two amounts. Give your answer in km and m.

explain.why: Made a slip in the m.
Took 413 m from 605 m the wrong way round.
Did not take 1 km away after regrouping.

questions.stem: Kumar has 13 pieces of rope of length 195 cm each. What is the total in m and cm?

explain.why: Lost a digit in the small part.
Left the answer as 2535 cm.
Used 1 m = 10 cm.

questions.stem: A total of 1 l 680 ml is divided equally into 3 parts. How many ml are in each part?

explain.why: Put a zero in the wrong place.
Divided by 2.
Divided by 4.

questions.stem: Nurul's full pot of soup has a total mass of 2.85 kg. After 3/4 of the contents are used, the total mass is 1.05 kg. What is the mass of the empty container, in grams?

explain.why: Multiplied the used mass by 3/4 instead of dividing.
Used the mass after using some contents as the empty mass.
Used the number of parts left instead of the whole.

solution: 3/4 of contents = 1800 g, so contents = 2400 g

questions.stem: A jug contains 6 l 750 ml of water. Arjun fills as many glasses of 120 ml as possible. How many glasses are filled completely?

explain.why: Counted the glass that is only partly filled.
Made a slip in the division.
Used 1 l = 100 ml.

questions.stem: The lengths of four things in Mei Ling's pencil case are: rope 57 cm, stick 59 cm, strip of paper 25 cm and leaf 8 cm. Which is the second shortest?

explain.why: Counted from the wrong end of the ordered list.
Gave the item at the other end of the list.
Gave the shortest instead of the second.

solution: Order from shortest to longest: 8 cm, 25 cm, 57 cm, 59 cm.
The second shortest is the strip of paper, 25 cm.

questions.stem: Shu Fen has a ribbon that is 48 cm long, a pencil that is 38 cm long and a wire that is 8 cm long. How much longer is the ribbon than the wire, in cm?

explain.why: Compared the shortest with the middle one.
Compared the longest with the middle one.
Added the two lengths.

questions.stem: Arjun measures a pencil with a ruler but starts from a mark that is not 0, as shown. What is the length of the pencil to the nearest cm?

explain.why: Rounded to the wrong whole number of centimetres.
Counted one gap too few or too many.
Read the right end of the line without subtracting the start mark.

solution: The line starts at 2 cm. Its right end is at about 13.8 cm.
Length = 13.8 - 2 = 11.8 cm, which is 12 cm to the nearest cm.

Only line A has right end - left end = 8 cm.
